text:
sam: Noticed an interesting failure mode on today's ensemble canary for ember-v1q (int4). When the mirror ensemble is enabled, some requests result in two different tool names being emitted by the two replicas, both syntactically valid JSON, which our router then executes in parallel. Leads to conflicting side-effects for the same logical request.

keiko: ugh. any examples?

sam: short example (mirrored outputs):
Replica A -> {"tool": "create_ticket", "args": {"title": "svc outage"}}
Replica B -> {"tool": "create_incident", "args": {"summary": "svc outage"}}
Both parsed fine but different tool semantics. We saw this hit twice in production-like load and it caused duplicate downstream entities.

dario: is this a quant artifact? or the ensemble merging strategy?

sam: likely both. Ember-v1q int4 has slightly shifted tokenization and sequencing under bursty streaming. The ensemble policy currently naively takes the first parseable result from any replica and forwards it. If replicas diverge, we have no consensus check.

keiko: proposed short-term: enforce replica consensus for tool name and args fingerprint before routing. If disagreement, mark as "conflict" and fall back to single-master (non-mirrored) execution or reject. That would avoid executing two incompatible tools concurrently.

dario: agree. For canary we should be conservative: 1) add consensus gate that requires identical tool name after normalization and args fingerprint; 2) log conflict sample and increase alerting to P1 if conflicts > 0.1% on canary.

sam: implemented a lightweight args fingerprint (normalize unicode NFKC, stable-key-order serialize, sha1). For canary (N=800) enabling consensus gate reduced conflicting tool executes from 0.8% -> 0.05% but increased apparent latency by ~18ms median due to waiting for both replicas.

keiko: acceptable for mirrored mode. But we also saw cases where replicas produced the same tool name but different arg shapes (schema mismatch). How do we handle that?

dario: treat as conflict as well. If tool name same but args schema differs (e.g., missing required fields or type mismatch), mark conflict and route to single-master or reject. We should prefer deterministic single-master behavior rather than heal heuristics.

mirror-bot: canary run 1777654340 updated: consensus gate enabled for ember-v1q int4 on 2% traffic.

sam: extra note: heal-vs-reject debate. Some teams want a sanitizer that fills missing args or maps synonyms; others prefer to fail loudly so we detect drift. For mirrored canary we should fail loud and capture. For broader rollout, maybe a watchdog that can attempt minimal heals with explicit audit logs.

keiko: telemetry additions: conflict_count, consensus_wait_ms, args_fingerprint_entropy, per-replica-tool-delta. Also record sdk_version and quant config so we can correlate.

dario: ops plan: 1) ship consensus gate to canary & enable detailed logging; 2) run 48h canary at 5% but with mirror on for small subset; 3) if conflict_rate < 0.2% and rollback_rate low we proceed; else revert mirror for int4.

sam: I'll open PR for consensus gate (canary-flagged) and add a small fuzz test in the structured-output harness that randomly perturbs token boundaries to exercise divergence.

keiko: add a dashboard panel showing conflicting-tool-executions by model+quant and a link to raw payloads (redact tokens).

canary-bot: snapshot after 2h (N=1200): conflict_rate 0.06%, consensus_wait_ms median 22ms, args_fingerprint_entropy slightly higher on int4 vs float32.

dario: promising. keep monitoring. If entropy keeps rising we should pause. For now consensus gate looks like the right safety net for mirrored ensembles on quantized models.

sam: thanks, will post PR link and test artifacts here.
